newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: INSTANT VIEW-S.Korea's April production, May CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-S.Korea's April production, May CPI.

text.p: Following are comments by analysts on South Korea's industrial output in April and consumer inflation in May, based on government figures released on Friday:
HAN SANG-CHOON, ECONOMIST AT DAEWOO RESEARCH INSTITUTE:
"April industrial output figures raise hopes of an imminent economic recovery. Despite the high growth in inventories, the prospects of recovery are bright because of improving global demand."
"The yen's rise -- and it is expected to rise to 100 to 105 (to) the dollar at the end of this year -- will help boost the nation's exports."
"The slowing consumer price index shows the economy is now near the bottom. Severe competition in distribution and falling raw material prices in global markets also helped price stability in May."
KIM KWANG-YUL, ECONOMIST AT DONGWON ECONOMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE:

"Output growth in April appears to be much higher than expected. That unmistakably shows the economy is about to rebound. But the recovery will take place gradually because of still high levels of inventories."
"Consumer inflation is likely be controlled within the government's target of 4.5 percent."
NAMUH RHEE, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT DONGBANG PEREGRINE SECURITIES:

"Most capital spending in the current cycle had been concentrated in capital-intensive industries, which means the current inventory adjustment process was being delayed as shown in the April figures."
"Inflation figures show asset deflation is going on. The CPI will be lower than 4.5 percent (this year)."
KIM SUNG-SHIK, ECONOMIST AT LG ECONOMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE:
"The low level of consumer inflation shows the typical cyclical point where an economic bottom is being touched. If the current trend holds, the CPI will be limited to below four percent this year."
"Given the high levels of inventories, the economic bottom will be hit in the third quarter of this year."
